prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance–Outbound Load Control Desk handoff; excludes aircraft loading. Custody continuous; monitored/task-authorized access. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) supplies flight data/Flight Cutoff Advisory to authoritative Baggage Control System (Velvet): validates assignments/cutoffs/allowances; records events/releases/dispositions; authorizes returns; reports missing/duplicate/delayed events. Reassignment requires approval; holds/missed cutoffs block release. Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit stages without reassociation; sends Oversize Exception Ticket to Image Resolution Desk. Bag Tag Printer produces durable unique tags/Calibration Witness Tag; replacements authorized. Transfer Bag Feeder accepts verified identity/onward-flight bags; sends Late Transfer Bag Card to Bag Reconciliation Station, which checks identities/counts/expected population, flags missing/duplicate/unmatched records, sends Bag Match Query to Airline Ramp Coordinator. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight): lanes/induction, Recovery Route Card, monitoring state/alarm reports. Induction Tray Conveyor meters/scans/spaces verified-route bags; interlocks stop feed. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel): tags/images; South Gate Scanner: Manual Rescan Receipt; healthy operation required. Operator/Image Resolution Desk records dispositions; inconclusive images require inspection/identity agreement; unresolved bags held. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) routes cleared bags/diverts unresolved; sends Chute Occupancy Note. Secondary Inspection Chute excludes unrelated bags. Security Duty Manager resolves holds/access/seals using Explosives Response Team’s Custody Seal Log/approved dispositions. Pebble (unspecified full name) secures response area. Returns require identity/outcome/authorization agreement. East Make-Up Conveyor: guarded/capacity-limited, identity-checked correct-flight transport. West Make-Up Conveyor: allocation/access/reconciliation. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) receives Airline Ramp Coordinator’s Carousel Release Slip; requires clearance/sequence/window/capacity/screening/destination. Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern): exceptions/holds/recovery/approvals. Maintenance Technician: isolation/accounting/calibration/faults. Restart requires personnel clear/guards/understood alarms/route; bypasses require maintenance approval. Coordinator verifies readable identity/current flight/security before loading. Desk accepts only consistent flight/count/status and physical-record agreement; discrepancies block acceptance. Departure requires recorded screening/custody/reconciliation/loading checks. Monitoring continuously covers throughput/availability/queues/screening/exceptions; conveyors’ stops/rates, sorter

New part:
S238: The Transfer Bag Feeder is monitored for feed rate, interruptions, and backlog against its scheduled demand.
S239: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is monitored for operating state, accumulation, and the time required to clear assigned work.
S240: The East Make-Up Conveyor and the West Make-Up Conveyor are assessed separately so that a local fault does not obscure the condition of the other conveyor.
S241: Tern reviews the operating dashboard and confirms that material service degradation has been assigned an owner and response priority.
S242: The Maintenance Technician investigates equipment faults that exceed the approved recovery interval and records the corrective action taken.
S243: The Security Duty Manager assesses any condition that could compromise screening coverage, security controls, or custody continuity.
S244: The Explosives Response Team is escalated to when an unresolved security condition requires its response under airport procedures.
S245: Service measures include availability, bags processed per operating interval, queue age, screening completion, and unresolved reconciliation differences.
S246: Thresholds and reporting intervals are established in the approved operating plan and reviewed against demand, flight schedules, and safety constraints.
S247: A degraded mode may be used only when the remaining equipment and procedures preserve required screening, traceability, custody, and reconciliation controls.
S248: Operations must suspend the affected activity when required controls cannot be maintained or when an unverified equipment state could misroute baggage.
S249: The Baggage Operations Supervisor coordinates escalation to maintenance, security, and airline operations according to the severity and operational impact of the condition.
S250: Return to service requires the fault to be corrected, required functional checks to pass, alarms to clear, and affected records to be reconciled.
S251: The responsible operational and technical personnel confirm that screening and custody controls are effective before normal routing resumes.
S252: The recovery is monitored at increased frequency until performance is stable and outstanding exceptions have been resolved or formally assigned.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
